mu_name_from: MuMain loads MODEL_GLOVES + i from GloveMale{i+1} (ZzzOpenData.cpp line 142), so file 09 is index 8, which openmu's 0.75 Armors.cs names the Brass Gloves. mu.db agrees: group 10 index 8, Player/GloveMale09.bmd.
why_this_one: Martin's and Harold's last +3 line, and the piece that finishes their shelf: with these five the wandering merchants sell all twenty-five of the lines Market.Wandering lists, where they sold ten this morning. See shared/Market.cs.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Armors.cs. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: ArmorInitializerBase.CreateGloves(number, name, dropLevel, defense, attackSpeed, durability, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, darkWizardClassLevel, darkKnightClassLevel, elfClassLevel). Slot 5, so the group is 10.
stats.defense_note: Points of defence, in the row and summed into Player.ArmourDefense by Wear - see shared/Rows.cs.
stats.attack_speed_note: Eight, which OpenMU adds to the character's AttackSpeed as a glove bonus. shared/Combat.cs takes speed off the weapon row alone, so this is recorded and unread.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are 0, 1, 0 - the Dark Knight alone. A hundred strength and thirty agility, the highest agility any built armour asks for.

sheet_from: Data/Player/gloves_10.OZJ (64x64), hide.jpg and boots_10b.ozt, from MuMain. The .bmd names gloves_10.jpg, hide.jpg and boots_10b.tga; 138 of the 148 triangles are on the first, 6 on hide and 4 on the ornament - the same four-triangle gold fan the armour and the boots wear.
sheet_note: gloves_10 is the pair of gauntlets from two sides: banded gold plates over the forearm with a studded knuckle and a dark seam between them. Mean (105, 91, 46) at chroma 59. hide is MU capping the openings, a solid black square, as on ArmorMale10. The set is a bright yellow gold and the sheets are the most saturated armour in the project: chroma 38 on the legs to 100 on the wing ornament, where the Bronze set runs 30 to 70 and the Plate set 3 to 8. Olive-green shading in the hollows, which is MU painting a warm metal's shadow cool.
material_note:
Four islands. Islands 2 and 3 are 72 each - the two gauntlets, gloves_10's 138 and hide's 6 - and take plate_steel. Islands 0 and 1 are two triangles each, boots_10b's 4: the gold fan at each wrist, brass.

The set is one colour and two materials, which is the thing it teaches. The plates take plate_steel - hammered, curved, roughness 0.68 - and the small ornaments on their own .OZT sheets take brass, which is cast at 0.44 with a coarser grain. Both are gold in MU's paint and the paint is not what decides: a material states how a thing was made, so a shell beaten to fit a chest and a fan of quills poured in a mould are two surfaces however alike their colour. It is the same reading the Pad Boots' fins got, made inside a single set for the first time.
material_overrides_why: plate_steel gives up its pull toward grey and a little of its polish, as on the Bronze set and for the same reason. Every sheet in this set says bright yellow gold - the most saturated armour in the project, chroma 38 to 100 - and plate_steel ships f0_desaturation 0.75, which took the gold out: cooked on 2026-09-21 the cuirass's base colour came out at saturation 0.21 from the art's 0.47 and the set read as grey steel with brass quills. Roughness 0.35 -> 0.46 comes with it, because on Bronze full saturation at the library's polish put hot glassy specular on the shoulder and hip. The alloy is still MU's paint; the material is still plate_steel.
